note: From OpenStreetMap's main API (13 October 2026), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks: two side platforms of about 88 m on the Buxton line, 2.1 m outside its two tracks (trains stop 12 m north of the station's point, so a two-car unit stands on them as they are and a four-car one once they're extended; a six-car one stands off the north end, as at a real short platform, which `longest` says), in a cutting just below the A6, which crosses at the platforms' east end on a skewed stone arch (drawn square to the line, 14 m wide) (Disley Tunnel proper begins about 90 m beyond it). Positive v is north. The halt's platform (towards Manchester) is on the south side, level with Station Approach, its car park and the station building; the far platform is reached by its own path down through the trees from the A6, so the way across is over the line on the A6. Views from above (docs/reference/aerial/disley.jpg). Photos (docs/reference/photos/disley: geograph 8405583, 8405581, 8405584, 8405582 and 8405574 DS Pugh 2026, 7686654 Stephen McKay 2024, 4293949 and 4293941 Mike Faherty 2014, 4252892 Nigel Thompson 2012, 5602883 Gerald England 2017): the station building a small white flat-roofed block whose roof overhangs the halt's platform; a small shelter on the far one; blue lamp columns, benches and garden planting; a low brick wall with gardens above it behind the far platform; a timber fence behind the halt's. The arch's span and height and the path's levels from the photos and the LIDAR, not survey. No canopy, kiosk, barriers, lifts or extension at the real station: the game's.
